newsitem.title: USA: Mining investors seeking reassurance on Peru.
newsitem.headline: Mining investors seeking reassurance on Peru.

text.p: Mining companies interested in doing business in Peru may be wary because of the current hostage crisis, but upon investigation will find the problem is an isolated event, mining executives said on Monday.

"At the very beginning they were worried about everything. But right now they realize it is a localized problem," said Carlos Diaz Canseco, General Manager of the National Society for Mining and Petroluem in Lima, Peru.

After addressing the National Western Mining Conference, he told Reuters potential investors probably have been asking about risk insurance, but are reassured when they discuss the issue with international companies now doing business in Peru.

Don East, of Knight Piesold and Co, a consulting firm, said companies not familiar with Peru will be a little nervous. But "The companies that have been working there and have established security - they will continue operating there," he said.
Canseco told the conference that Peru accounts for 2.5 percent of the world's gold production and 13.1 percent of its silver production.
